name: Riff

status.note: Called Databutton until 2025; the Oslo company behind it, still Databutton AS, now sells Riff as a platform for AI agents in industrial operations.

summary: An Oslo-built AI builder, formerly Databutton, whose agent writes React and FastAPI apps and configures ERP-connected agents for procurement and operations teams in manufacturing.
intro: Riff builds two kinds of things from a chat with its building assistant, the Riff agent. Apps are screens people open, such as dashboards, forms and portals. Agents are workers with a trigger (a schedule, an inbound email, a new ERP record) that do a defined job, such as chasing suppliers for unconfirmed purchase orders, and escalate what they can’t decide. For apps, the Riff agent writes a React and TypeScript frontend and a Python FastAPI backend on serverless PostgreSQL, shows it in a live preview, and keeps a task board of what it is doing; a code editor shows every file. **Deploy** publishes to `username.riff.works/app-name` after checks for the subdomain, permissions and basic security.

Each app has development and production environments with separate databases, environment variables and secrets, so a secret can point at a test ERP endpoint while building and the live one in production. What sets Riff apart from general app builders is its focus: native connectors for SAP S/4HANA, Oracle ERP Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Infor LN and M3, which call the ERP’s own business functions so its validation and audit apply; a shared Context library the agents learn from; and MCP access for Copilot, Claude and other agents. It is sold through demos and forward-deployed engineers rather than self-serve plans, and Riff says it is incentivized on the customer’s results rather than charging hours.
strengths: Built for ERP work: maintained connectors to major ERPs, and agents act through the system’s own business functions with every action logged
Apps and agents in one workspace, sharing integrations, secrets and a Context library
Separate development and production databases and secrets, plus pre-deployment security and integration review skills
A conventional stack (React, TypeScript, FastAPI, PostgreSQL) and a code editor that shows every generated source file
limits: Narrow focus: Riff is now built for procurement and operations teams in manufacturing, and its docs, playbooks and connectors target ERP work
No public pricing: access starts with a demo, and delivery is a consulting-style engagement
Deployed apps are hosted by Riff, at `riff.works` URLs or a custom domain
Every app uses the same stack, so teams standardized on another framework or language get no choice

worksWith.how: stores each app’s data in serverless

story: Trygve Karper, Martin Røed and Viral Shah met at Cognite, the Norwegian industrial data company, where they saw how hard it was for data scientists and analysts to turn ideas into tools their colleagues could use. They founded Databutton in Oslo in 2021: a browser workspace for building and deploying interactive data apps in Python, helped by an AI assistant called Databutler that could use models such as GPT-4 and frameworks such as Streamlit and LangChain. In September 2023 it raised a €4.8 million seed round.

Databutton grew into a full-stack AI app builder and, as Riff, raised a $16 million Series A led by Northzone in October 2025, bringing its funding to $21 million. It had more than 150,000 users, at companies including Twilio and Cognite, and pitched production-grade apps with real data connections over demo-quality vibe coding.

By 2026 Riff had narrowed its focus to industrial companies, where its team had spent years building Cognite. It now sells AI agents for order handling, procurement, logistics, production and aftermarket service, built on the same app and agent builder, and says more than 15 enterprises run its agents in production.

choices.choice: Start from data and the people who know the business
choices.why: The founders had watched domain experts at Cognite struggle to turn ideas into tools, so Databutton aimed at people with ideas and only a basic understanding of code, with an AI assistant guiding each step in the browser.

choices.choice: Connect to real systems, not demo data
choices.why: Riff pointed to the 95% of enterprise AI initiatives that fail, and set itself apart from other vibe coding tools with native data connections and secure, production-grade infrastructure built into the builder.

choices.choice: Act through the ERP’s own functions
choices.why: Its agents create purchase orders and post receipts by calling the ERP’s business functions, so the system’s validation and audit apply to every action, under rules set by IT.

€4.8M seed; the Databutler AI assistant in beta
$16M Series A led by Northzone, as Riff, in October
Refocused on AI agents for industrial operations; 15+ enterprises in production
